label: Exchange auction
definition: Trading on a power exchange in which orders for each delivery period are collected until gate closure and cleared together in one run, giving one price per period.

label: Exchange continuous trading
definition: Trading on a power exchange in which an order is matched as soon as a compatible order arrives from the other side, so trading continues until shortly before delivery and each trade has its own price.

label: Exchange-traded derivative
definition: A standardised futures or options contract listed on an exchange and cleared through a clearing house, for delivery or financial settlement over a future period such as a month, quarter or season.

label: Over-the-counter (bilateral) contract
definition: A contract agreed directly between two parties, or through a broker, rather than on an exchange order book. It may be physically delivered or settled financially.

label: System operator ancillary service
definition: A service that the system operator procures or requires from generation, demand or storage to keep the transmission system secure, for example frequency response, reserve, voltage support, stability, constraint management or restoration.

label: Balancing Mechanism
definition: The system operator's main real-time balancing tool: participants submit offers to export more or import less, and bids to do the opposite, and the system operator accepts those it needs.

label: DSO flexibility service
definition: A service that a distribution network operator buys from flexibility providers to manage its own network, for example to defer reinforcement or to cover outages. DNOs must publish how they procure these services.

label: Capacity mechanism
definition: A scheme that pays providers to commit capacity that will be available when the system is under stress, so that enough reliable capacity exists to meet future demand.

label: Revenue support scheme
definition: A government-backed scheme that reduces long-term revenue risk for eligible projects, for example by paying the difference between an agreed strike price and a market reference price.
